model.source: docs/ernie55/iqr-v4-layers.json (measured per-class bytes x checkpoint counts)

scenarios.note: TP8, the latent and index caches replicated on every rank (as glm5next does: one latent head); with DCP (story 6) they shard 1/8. free_per_card is what is left for KV, speculative buffers and prefill arena.
scenarios.socket_note: all eight cards means a production model already on the other socket's cards must be unloaded first: a planned maintenance window

scenarios.link_note: CONDITIONAL ESTIMATE, not a bound: it assumes routing spreads uniformly over the experts and a link throughput that is NOT measured here (25 and 50 GB/s are stated assumptions); a token can pick more streamed experts than the expectation. The only hard bound is the all-streamed traffic figure (10 experts a layer, every one from host); the hot-expert profile (expert-tiered placement) is what would tighten it, and no routing distribution of the real model has been measured
scenarios.note: the four cards of one socket are free and at most 4 cards may be busy: this variant fits such a window and is the CHEAPEST way to run ERNIE for a first real-weight measurement

the host pool is capped at 32 GiB unless the machine's free memory says otherwise; the GPU window allowance is memguard's gpu_window_ok_gib. At TP8 on all cards no expert is streamed and host RAM is not on the path.

fp8_baseline.note: the figure of the earlier plan: block FP8 is not a Radiance 2.x serving format, so this configuration cannot exist; it is kept to show what the target changes

assumptions.kv_formula: 7 MLA layers x ((512+64) x 2 + 132) bytes + 37 HCA layers x 1024/128 bytes, per token, plus a fixed 128-token window a sequence in each HCA layer; bf16 cache; replicated tensors counted: routers, mHC, indexer wk and weights_proj, latent norm, compressor APE (the compressor kv/gate projections are treated as sharded)
